data.title: Challenger Turns Down Daiichi Life’s Revised $4.4 Billion Takeover Offer
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Challenger Ltd. rejected a revised A$6.5 billion ($4.4 billion) takeover offer from Daiichi Life Group Inc., marking the Japanese insurer’s second rejection in a month.

data.title: New York FX: Dollar Rises as Pound Hits Near One-Year Low After UK Inflation Data
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, the dollar rose against most G10 currencies as traders maintained bets on further Federal Reserve rate hikes despite a sharp drop in oil prices. The pound fell to its lowest level in nearly a year.

The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index gained 0.3%, rebounding after a decline on Tuesday, while Brent crude fell below $92 a barrel.

Sterling fell as much as 0.6% to $1.3136 against the dollar. UK inflation data released Wednesday prompted traders to reduce bets on further Bank of England rate hikes.

The euro fell 0.2% to $1.0979. The dollar was little changed at 159.32 yen, while the Australian dollar fell 0.2% to $0.6721.

data.title: Satya Nadella: Nvidia Board to Decide Next Steps After Jensen Huang's Resignation
data.description: According to Jin10, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said he wanted to give former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang space to sort things out, adding that Nvidia's board would decide what happens next.

data.title: Landus Says Former CEO Misused Funds for Vacation Home, Plane
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Landus says former CEO Matt Carstens misused funds for a vacation home and plane. When Carstens stepped down, the board of Iowa’s largest farm cooperative expressed gratitude for his “forward-thinking” leadership.

data.title: FedWatch Puts Odds of a 25-Basis-Point December Hike at 92.7%
data.description: According to Jin10, CME's FedWatch tool put the probability of a 25-basis-point Fed rate hike in December at 92.7%, compared with 7.3% for a 50-basis-point hike; by January next year, the probabilities of cumulative hikes of 25, 50, and 75 basis points were 26.7%, 68.1%, and 5.2%, respectively.

data.title: Palo Alto Networks Strikes $4.5 Billion Applied Compute Deal; Shares Jump 8% on Earnings
data.description: According to CNBC, Palo Alto Networks shares rose more than 8% after the cybersecurity company beat fiscal first-quarter estimates and agreed to a $4.5 billion all-stock deal for AI startup Applied Compute. Adjusted earnings per share were $1.05, versus 97 cents expected, while revenue was $3.44 billion, above the $3.31 billion estimate. Palo Alto raised its fiscal 2027 outlook, forecasting adjusted earnings per share of $4.26 to $4.30 and revenue of $14.52 billion to $14.57 billion.

data.description: According to Jin10, Moody's expects deficits to remain above 6% of GDP throughout the next decade without major policy changes, keeping federal debt on an upward trajectory.

data.description: Alberta banned AI data center development on irrigated land and set a 600-meter rule, according to Bloomberg. data.title: U.S. Treasury Prices Rise as Steady 20-Year Auction Supports Longer-Dated Bonds
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, U.S. Treasury prices rose during Wednesday’s U.S. trading session, led by longer-dated bonds, as demand at a 20-year auction remained steady. The 2-year/10-year and 5-year/30-year spreads moved near their session lows. The auction’s yield was in line with pre-sale trading, extending the earlier flattening of the yield curve.

Most of the gains came during the U.S. morning, when Treasuries drew support after spot stocks turned lower shortly after opening. Stocks later rebounded, led by technology shares. Shortly after 3 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time, Treasury yields hovered near session lows, with longer-term yields down as much as 5 basis points. The 2-year/10-year and 5-year/30-year spreads narrowed by 4 basis points and 1.5 basis points, respectively. The 10-year yield was down about 4 basis points at 5.07%.

The new 20-year Treasury notes were awarded at a 5.459% yield, below the record high set in October. Primary dealers received 13.1% of the auction, up from the previous sale; direct bidders received 26.7%, while indirect bidders received 60.2%. Ahead of the auction, Treasuries gained as the S&P 500 fell to a four-month low and oil prices declined. WTI crude futures settled 3.2% lower, falling below $85 a barrel for the first time since late August.

Demand for upside hedges reappeared in the Treasury options market, mainly through December-expiring 10-year Treasury 107.00 calls. Several March SOFR options structures traded actively, with positions aimed at a decline in the rate-hike premium priced into expectations for the Fed’s next several policy meetings.

As of 4:23 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time, the 2-year Treasury yield was little changed at 4.8042%; the 5-year yield fell 2.7 basis points to 4.8877%; the 10-year yield fell 3.8 basis points to 5.0683%; and the 30-year yield fell 4.7 basis points to 5.411%. The 5-year/30-year spread narrowed about 2.1 basis points to 52.14 basis points, and the 2-year/10-year spread narrowed about 4.1 basis points to 26.2 basis points.

data.title: Seaport Research, Morgan Stanley Flag Nvidia Financing Shift as Risk for CoreWeave, Neoclouds
data.description: According to CNBC, CoreWeave and Iren fell around 3% in afternoon trading Wednesday, while Nebius rose around 2%, as investors anticipated tighter financing from Nvidia. The stocks’ gains after Nvidia’s earnings call on Tuesday faded. Analysts focused on changes to Nvidia’s financial footnotes, which indicate that commitments to neoclouds depend on their securing financing for data center infrastructure and may be reduced or canceled if they do not. Interim CEO Colette Kress said Nvidia’s guarantees would begin at the specified point and would not remain in place if construction were delayed. Morgan Stanley credit analyst Lindsay Tyler kept her estimate of Nvidia’s debt adjustments and contingent obligations at around $170 billion by the end of 2028, but lowered her forecast for deployments to 4 gigawatts from 5 gigawatts. She cited neocloud commitments falling to $32 billion from $36 billion quarter over quarter. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said Wednesday that a half-percentage-point rate increase at the December meeting may be necessary to curb inflation.

data.title: Saifedean Ammous Says AI May Be Overvalued, Bitcoin Could Soon Rally Independently
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing Bitcoin Magazine, Saifedean Ammous, author of “The Bitcoin Standard,” said on the Bitcoin Magazine T.V. (BMTV) program that Anthropic and OpenAI may ultimately be severely overvalued and questioned whether current AI valuations are justified. Ammous said Bitcoin is in a bear market but may be near the bottom, and he expects it to soon begin a rally of its own. He argued that Bitcoin and AI are not competitors, describing Bitcoin as the only thing AI cannot increase in supply. The discussion also covered fiat inflation, Federal Reserve rate hikes and debt pressures, Argentina’s inflation, stablecoins, AI capital spending, and the effects of a K-shaped economy on ordinary households.
